faqs.question: How long should a Halloween paragraph for my girlfriend be?
faqs.answer: Aim for 100 to 200 words, which reads in under a minute: 110 words takes about 45 seconds aloud. Under 25 words it is a text, and past 300 it becomes a letter.

faqs.question: Is a long Halloween message the same as a love letter?
faqs.answer: No. A long message is one block of about 100 to 200 words built around a single memory or job, like thanking her or promising next year. A love letter usually runs 300 words or more, with an opening, several parts and a sign-off.

faqs.question: Can I send a long Halloween message to my girlfriend by text?
faqs.answer: Yes, but plain SMS splits it: a 110-word paragraph is about 600 characters, or 4 linked segments, and one emoji drops each segment to 67 characters, making about 9. WhatsApp or iMessage sends it as one bubble.

faqs.question: What should I write if we only started dating a few weeks ago?
faqs.answer: Keep it light and short, closer to 60 words than 150, and skip big declarations. The costume hype (paragraph 4) or the laugh (paragraph 8) trimmed by half suits an early relationship better than a memory or a promise.

faqs.question: How do I say sorry to my girlfriend on Halloween without ruining the night?
faqs.answer: Send the apology within a day of what happened, before the Halloween plans, and name exactly what went wrong and how it landed on her. In a 275-couple study, partners who felt understood held less unforgiveness, so being specific matters more than being long.

faqs.question: What do I write to my girlfriend if she is working on Halloween night?
faqs.answer: Write for her break, not her start: one thing waiting for her at home, one line of respect for the work, and a new date for your own Halloween. Paragraph 6 runs 101 words and sits on a single phone screen.

faqs.question: Should I post my Halloween paragraph about her on Instagram?
faqs.answer: Only if she has read it privately first and is happy for it to be public. A caption can hold 2,200 characters, but only the first lines show before "more", and anything about her health or job stays private.

faqs.question: Can I copy these paragraphs word for word?
faqs.answer: Copy the structure, not the brackets. Each paragraph was written for this page and has 1 to 4 bracketed details; left generic, it reads like a template, so swap every bracket for something nobody else would know.

faqs.question: When is Halloween in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Halloween is 31 October every year: a Saturday in 2026 and a Sunday in 2027. That matters for paragraph 10, which promises a plan for next year's date.

faqs.question: Can I send my paragraph with a voice note?
faqs.answer: Yes. The premium Halloween page takes a voice note up to 60 seconds next to a letter of up to 3,000 characters, so you can read the paragraph aloud and attach it. The regular page takes a letter and up to six photos but no voice note.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Paragraph for Girlfriend: 10 Long Messages With a Job

A good Halloween paragraph for your girlfriend runs 100 to 200 words, does one job (thank, apologise, remember, hype, comfort or promise) and hangs on a detail nobody else knows. That is longer than the typical note: on 214 SubhSandesh miss-you pages the median letter runs 88 words (another template, two months of data), and 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages get opened on phones. Below: 10 original paragraphs by job, channel limits and editing rules.

## What is a Halloween paragraph for a girlfriend?

A Halloween paragraph is one block of 100 to 200 words, sent near 31 October, that tells one small story and lands one feeling. It sits between a sub-25-word text and a 300-word letter. Across four experiments with 560 participants, [Pintea and Ray (British Journal of Psychology, 2025)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12256725) found that displaying memory for specific details conveyed more value, yet people underused it unless prompted.

## 10 Halloween paragraphs for your girlfriend, by job

Each runs about 100 words. Swap every bracket for something real.

### 1. Thank her (send the morning after)

> I keep thinking about how much of last night was you. You found the costumes, remembered [the neighbor's kids] would knock at six, and made one bowl of [mini chocolate bars] last the whole evening. I turned up and took credit for one lopsided pumpkin. So this is the credit going where it belongs. Thank you for turning an ordinary [Saturday] into a night I'll still be describing in December. Thank you for laughing when my fake blood ran into my collar. Mostly, thank you for wanting to do any of this with me. Next year, the planning is mine, start to finish.

### 2. Apologise and reassure her (send within a day)

> I've been thinking about [Thursday], and I owe you more than the quick sorry I mumbled. You'd looked forward to [the haunted maze] for weeks, and I let work eat the evening without telling you until it was too late to make other plans. That wasn't fair, and I could see it stung. I won't promise it never happens again, because you'd know that's a line. What I can promise: the tickets for [Friday] are booked, my phone goes in the glovebox, and the only thing I'm checking is whether you're scared. You matter more than my inbox, and I'll show you.

### 3. Remember your first Halloween together (send before you go out)

> Do you still think about our first Halloween? You wore [a very serious Wednesday Addams look] and I showed up in [a fitted-sheet ghost] that kept sliding off one shoulder. We left [Sam's party] early, sat on the curb with a bag of [candy corn] neither of us liked, and talked until the street lights clicked off. I didn't know then that I'd remember the exact song drifting out of the window. I do. Every October since, that curb is the first thing I picture. Whatever we do tonight, I'm glad it started there, with you laughing at my sheet.

### 4. Hype her costume (send an hour before she leaves)

> Before you head out, I need to say this properly. You spent [three evenings] on that costume, stitching [the cape lining] by hand while I watched a film and offered nothing useful, and it shows. Nobody at that party will have thought harder about their look, and nobody will wear it better. I love that you commit to things all the way, [glue-gun burns] and all. Walk into that party like it was thrown for you, because tonight it was. Take a photo before anyone spills a drink on you, and send it to me first. I'm so proud of you, [Name].

### 5. Comfort her when you are apart (send late afternoon)

> It's strange spending Halloween [800 miles] apart, and I know it's harder on you, in a city where nobody on your street decorates. So here's our plan. At [9pm your time] we both put on the worst horror film we can find, video call on mute, and I'll provide commentary by text. I've bought the same [peanut butter cups] you have, so technically we're sharing. Distance doesn't make this night less ours; it just makes the commute longer. [Fifty-two] days until I see you. I'm counting them the way kids count down to the thirty-first, out loud and very badly.

### 6. Comfort her on a night shift (send for her break)

> I know you're on shift tonight while the rest of the world is in costume, and I know how tired you were when you left. I wanted something waiting on your phone for your break. The house is quiet, your [pumpkin] is lit in the window so you'll see it when you pull in, and there's a bowl of [soup] in the fridge saved for you. You do hard, important work on nights most people get to forget about. I admire it more than I say. Halloween can wait until [Sunday]. We'll do the film and the candy then, just us.

### 7. Comfort her when she is ill (send early)

> I'm sorry you're stuck in bed on Halloween; you were so looking forward to [the party]. For the record, a blanket over your head counts as a ghost costume, and you've never looked better in one. Here's what's happening: I'm leaving [ginger ale, crackers and the good tissues] at your door at [six], then staying out of your way unless you want company. You don't need to reply to this. Rest is the only plan tonight. When you're better, we'll have our own Halloween, late and on your terms, and you get to pick the scariest film we own, no arguments.

### 8. Make her laugh (send mid-evening)

> Confession: I tried to carve a cat into our pumpkin to impress you, and it now looks like a potato that has seen something. I've named it [Gerald]. Gerald is on the porch judging the trick-or-treaters, and two of them have asked if he's okay. Also, the bag of candy I hid "for the kids" is mostly wrappers now, and I'm blaming the ghost in our hallway. I'm telling you because nobody makes Halloween as fun as you do, and the whole time I was ruining that pumpkin I was picturing you laughing. Come home soon. Gerald misses you. So do I.

### 9. Reassure her before a party of strangers (send while she dresses)

> I know you're a little nervous about tonight because you'll barely know anyone at [Jordan's]. Here's what to expect: [Jordan] will explain his fog machine for twenty minutes, [Priya] will ask where you found your costume, and I'll be next to you the whole time. If you want to leave, touch your ear and we'll go, no questions asked. You don't have to win anyone over. They'll like you because I've been talking about you for months, and they're curious who made me this happy. Honestly, the part I'm most excited about is walking through that door with you, [Name].

### 10. Promise her next Halloween (send last thing on 31 October)

> Next year the thirty-first lands on a [Sunday], and I've decided it's ours. No parties we feel we have to show up to, no rushing between houses. I'm promising you a slow day: pancakes shaped roughly like pumpkins, the [pumpkin patch] you keep bringing up, and costumes we actually plan together instead of panicking the night before. I'm writing it down so you can hold me to it. A year from now I want to be next to you, both in ridiculous outfits, laughing about how this year went. That isn't a big promise. It's just the one I most want to keep.

## Halloween paragraph length by channel: text, Instagram, page

Here is how 110 words fare on four channels. SMS is the strict one.

| Channel | Hard limit | Comfortable length | A 110-word paragraph |
|---|---|---|---|
| Plain SMS | 160 characters per segment; 70 once an emoji appears | 60 to 110 words | ~600 characters: 4 segments, 9 with an emoji |
| WhatsApp or iMessage | No practical text limit | 100 to 150 words | One bubble she can reread |
| Instagram caption | 2,200 characters, 30 hashtags | 100 to 150 words | Fits; first lines show before "more" |
| Premium Halloween page letter | 3,000 characters | 150 to 200 words | Fits twice over |

Limits: [Twilio's SMS character-limit guide](https://www.twilio.com/docs/glossary/what-sms-character-limit) and [Meta's Instagram API reference](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/instagram-platform/instagram-graph-api/reference/ig-user/media), checked October 2026. Plain SMS is the worst home for a paragraph, so drop the emoji or use a messaging app. Caption only what she has read privately.

## How do you edit a Halloween paragraph so it sounds like you?

- **Keep the order.** Start where the memory starts and end in the present. In [Vanaken and Hermans (Memory & Cognition, 2021)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC7886714), 107 listeners offered more support to coherent narrators; chronology and theme mattered most, and only for positive memories.
- **Name the hurt before the promise.** Among [275 couples (Yilmaz and colleagues, Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 2026)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12719928), partners who felt understood held less unforgiveness after a hurt, a correlation rather than proof.
- **Read it aloud.** 110 words takes about 45 seconds; if you stumble, she will too.

## Turning your paragraph into a Halloween page

On a page, your paragraph becomes the letter after the haunted-house steps. Pages average 11.1 views, rereads included.

The [regular Halloween card page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) is a 5-minute build: your letter plus six photos, read under a flashlight in the attic. The [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium), about 10 minutes, adds letters to 3,000 characters, voice notes to 60 seconds, 12 photos and a time lock. For distance, the [miss-you page](https://subhsandesh.in/missyou-gf) fits; 86.4% of those 214 pages hold one or more written memories.

## When a long Halloween paragraph is the wrong move

Two weeks in, 150 words of feelings can feel like pressure; a short text is safer. At a loud party she will not read it, so send before or after.

After a real fight, paragraph 2 backs up an apology said in person but does not replace it. A page also needs her phone or laptop; if she is beside you on 31 October, say it out loud.

## Sources

- Pintea and Ray, *British Journal of Psychology*, 27 February 2025.
- Yilmaz and colleagues, *Journal of Marital and Family Therapy*, January 2026.
- Vanaken and Hermans, *Memory & Cognition*, February 2021.
- Twilio, "What is the SMS character limit?", checked October 2026.
- Meta for Developers, "IG User Media" reference, checked October 2026.
